description.narrative: Access to Finance Rwanda (AFR) is a Rwandan non-profit company limited by guarantee (CLG) established with support from DFID in 2010 and with the core objective of stimulating the development of the financial sector and increasing financial inclusion by removing systemic barriers that hinder access to financial services among poor households, women and youth in Rwanda. The Swedish contribution supports implementation of Access to Finance Rwanda’s strategy for the period 2021 – 2025. Access to Finance Rwanda’s overarching strategy goal is to support a financial sector that delivers real value to poor people and marginalized groups, including women, youth and refugees, by increasing access and usage of appropriate and affordable financial services, while at the same time contributing to unlock more inclusive growth patterns across the economy, generating economic opportunities for millions of Rwandans, particularly among poor households. The intervention will be implemented in close collaboration with private sector actors, the government of Rwanda and other non-profit organizations.

Access to Finance Rwanda (AFR) är ett rwandiskt icke-vinstdrivande företag som med ekonomiskt stöd från DIFD etablerades i Rwanda 2010 och vars huvudmål är att stimulera utvecklingen av den rwandiska finanssektorn samt bidra till en ökad tillgång till finansiella tjänster bland fattiga hushåll, kvinnor och ungdomar i Rwanda. Det svenska bidraget avser stödja genomförandet av Access to Finance Rwandas strategi för perioden 2021 - 2025. Access to Finance Rwandas övergripande strategimål är att genom en systemansats bidra till en finanssektor som tillhandahåller finansiella tjänster som gynnar fattiga människor och marginaliserade grupper, såsom kvinnor, ungdomar och flyktingar, samtidigt som den bidrar till mer inkluderande tillväxtmönster som skapar inkomst- och sysselsättningsmöjligheter, i synnerhet för fattiga hushåll. Insatsen kommer att genomföras i nära samarbete med privata aktörer, regeringen och icke-vinstdrivande organisationer.

Access to Finance Rwanda (AFR) overarching objective is to contribute to the development of a diversified and inclusive financial sector that underpins national efforts toward enhanced resilience, sustainable livelihoods, and broad-based economic transformation in Rwanda.
AFRs aims to facilitate the establishment of a financial ecosystem that delivers demonstrable value to the national economy and its citizens, with particular emphasis on populations that remain unserved.
Key outcomes of AFRs work include expanding access to and encouraging the effective use of relevant, affordable, and high-quality financial products and services by women and marginalized groups, thereby fostering greater financial inclusion and socio-economic empowerment. At the same time, AFR aims to improve the availability and uptake of financial and long-term capital solutions for enterprises operating in underserved yet high-potential sectors such as agriculture with the goal of driving job creation, enhancing productivity, and supporting environmental sustainability.
Through these interventions, AFR seeks to align with national development priorities and contribute meaningfully to Rwandas inclusive growth agenda.

description.narrative:
Access to Finance Rwanda has since 2015 been one of Sidas flagship market development programmes in Rwanda. It has delivered measurable impact during these 10 years. Generally, AFR has played a catalytic role in advancing Rwandas financial inclusion agenda since its start in 2010.
Through targeted interventions, AFR has facilitated access to financial services for over 4.5 million individuals, contributing to the national inclusion rate increase from 48% in 2008 to 96% in 2024. AFR has supported the design and implementation of key national schemes, including Rwandas first national long-term savings scheme Ejo Heza with 3.5 million contributors, and the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme covering over 600 000 farmers. It also enabled the establishment of Rwandas first interoperable digital payment system, expanding digital usage to 1.5 million users and digitising government transfers for 600 000 recipients. Furthermore, AFR produces the national FinScope surveys that have informed national policy and regulatory frameworks in the financial sector.
